metaDescription: Private Bangkok to Pattaya transfer by Alphard, Vellfire or Camry. Fixed price with fuel, tolls and a 10-hour day included. Book 24/7 on WhatsApp.
h1: Bangkok to Pattaya, in quiet luxury
intro: Pattaya is the beach city most Bangkok visitors reach for first, and the road there is one of the best in the country. Your chauffeur collects you at your door, takes the motorway east and delivers you to your hotel, villa or yacht berth without a single change of vehicle.

sections.h2: The drive: Motorway 7, door to door
paragraphs: From central Bangkok the route usually joins Motorway 7, the Bangkok–Chonburi motorway, which runs almost uninterrupted to the edge of Pattaya. It is a wide, well-lit toll road with several service areas, so a coffee or restroom stop is easy to arrange without losing time. Highway 34, the Bang Na–Trat road, is the alternative your chauffeur may choose if the motorway is backed up.

In normal conditions the journey takes around two to two and a half hours for roughly 150 km. Friday afternoons and holiday weekends can stretch that, which is exactly when a reclining captain's chair and a driver who knows the shortcuts out of Sukhumvit earn their keep.

Beyond its nightlife reputation, Pattaya has grown into a resort city with headland hotels, beach clubs, marinas and championship golf. Pratumnak Hill and Wong Amat attract travellers who prefer quieter beaches, while Jomtien stretches south with long promenades and family-friendly condominiums.

Culture is closer than many expect. The all-teak Sanctuary of Truth is a genuine architectural marvel, Nong Nooch Tropical Garden spreads over a vast landscaped estate, and Koh Larn lies a short boat ride from Bali Hai Pier for a day of clearer water.

sections.h2: Transfer or a full day with your driver
paragraphs: Pattaya is priced on our Eastern Seaboard tier, which includes up to ten hours with the car and chauffeur. That means a one-way transfer can become a relaxed day trip: drive down in the morning, lunch on the coast, visit the viewpoint at sunset and return to Bangkok the same evening.

If you are staying several nights, many guests book the outbound transfer, then a separate car on the day of departure. Your chauffeur can also continue on to Sattahip, Rayong or U-Tapao Airport if your plans change; simply message us on WhatsApp.

sections.h2: Why a private chauffeur suits this route
paragraphs: Public buses and shared vans stop at terminals, not hotel lobbies, and taxis rarely have room for golf bags or several large suitcases. An Alphard or Vellfire swallows luggage for a family or a small group, with Wi-Fi-friendly quiet and climate control throughout.

Everything is agreed before you travel: one fixed price, fuel, motorway tolls and the driver's time included, with the rate table below showing each vehicle. There is no meter to watch and no negotiating on arrival.

Business guests heading to conference hotels or the industrial estates of the Eastern Seaboard often treat the motorway hours as a quiet office, while couples simply arrive rested. If you would like a coffee stop, a detour to Bang Saen beach or a call at a supermarket before reaching your villa, mention it and your chauffeur will build it into the plan.

title: Bangkok to Hua Hin Private Transfer by Chauffeur
metaDescription: Bangkok to Hua Hin by private chauffeur: a fixed-price, door-to-door drive down the Royal Coast with fuel and tolls included. Book 24/7 on WhatsApp.
h1: To Hua Hin, along the Royal Coast
intro: Hua Hin has been Thailand's royal seaside retreat for a century, and it still feels more measured than the resorts to the east. The drive south takes a little over three hours, and in the back of an Alphard it becomes a calm prelude to a long weekend.

paragraphs: Leaving Bangkok, your chauffeur heads south-west on Rama II Road, then joins Phetkasem Road, Highway 4, through Phetchaburi and down the coast. Rama II has had long-running roadworks and can be slow at peak times, so your driver will judge the departure window and, when it helps, use the alternative approach via Phetkasem from the western suburbs.

Expect around three to three and a half hours for roughly 200 km. A natural halfway pause is Phetchaburi, known for its hilltop palace and its traditional desserts, or one of the large fuel-station rest areas along Highway 4.

sections.h2: A resort town with royal roots
paragraphs: Hua Hin grew around the railway and the summer palace of Klai Kangwon, which remains a royal residence. Its beaches are long and gently shelving, its hotels range from historic colonial-style properties to secluded pool villas, and its golf courses are among the most respected in Thailand.

Evenings centre on the night market and, from Friday to Sunday, on Cicada Market with its art stalls and live music. Khao Takiab, at the southern end of the main beach, offers a hilltop temple and a wide view back over the bay.

Food is a quiet highlight. Seafood restaurants built on wooden piers along Naresdamri Road serve the morning's catch, and the town's red-and-cream railway station, with its ornate royal waiting pavilion, is one of the most photographed in the country.

Hua Hin sits on our long-distance tier, so you can choose a one-way transfer or a full day trip with the chauffeur waiting while you lunch, play a round or visit Maruekhathaiyawan Palace. The rate table below lists both options for every vehicle.
Families often appreciate the cabin space on this route: three hours is long enough that legroom, a quiet ride and a driver happy to stop when the children need a break make a real difference.

Let us know about golf bags, surfboards for Khao Takiab or a pram when you book on WhatsApp, and we will match the vehicle to the luggage. If you are flying in, we can collect you directly from Suvarnabhumi or Don Mueang and head south without stopping in the city.

Golfers are particularly well served. Several of the area's best-known courses, including the historic Royal Hua Hin Golf Course beside the railway, are within a short drive of town, and on the day-trip rate your chauffeur can shuttle you between hotel and tee time without any need to call a taxi.

title: Bangkok to Cha-am Private Transfer & Day Trips
metaDescription: Private chauffeur from Bangkok to Cha-am's quiet beach resorts. Fixed price, fuel and tolls included, transfer or day trip. Book 24/7 on WhatsApp.
h1: Cha-am: the calmer side of the coast
intro: Cha-am lies just north of Hua Hin and is where many Bangkok families escape for a weekend of seafood and sea breezes. It is a little closer, a little quieter and home to some of the region's largest beachfront resorts.

paragraphs: The usual route follows Rama II Road out of Bangkok before joining Phetkasem Road, Highway 4, which carries you past Phetchaburi and straight into Cha-am. For approximately 175 km, allow around two and a half to three hours, a little more if you leave on a Friday afternoon.

Phetchaburi is the obvious place to break the journey. The hilltop palace of Phra Nakhon Khiri overlooks the town, and the nearby Tham Khao Luang cave, with its shafts of light falling on Buddha images, is a striking detour of under an hour.

Cha-am's long beach is lined with casuarina trees, deckchairs and seafood stalls, and it feels distinctly Thai at weekends. Many international visitors use it as a peaceful base, with large resorts set on wide gardens and easy access to Hua Hin's restaurants about half an hour away.

For families, the area has a run of themed attractions along Phetkasem Road, including Santorini Park and the Swiss Sheep Farm. History lovers should not miss Maruekhathaiyawan Palace, an elegant seaside teak residence built for King Rama VI.

Golfers will find several well-regarded courses between Cha-am and Hua Hin, and the town's flat beach road is pleasant for an early walk or cycle before the heat arrives. Evenings are relaxed: a sunset drink, a long dinner and an early night are very much the local rhythm.

If you prefer to dine in Hua Hin one evening, a short return run along Highway 4 can be arranged on WhatsApp.

title: Bangkok to Pranburi Private Transfer by Chauffeur
metaDescription: Private transfer from Bangkok to Pranburi's boutique beach resorts and Sam Roi Yot. Fixed price, fuel and tolls included. Book 24/7 via WhatsApp.
h1: Pranburi, beyond the busy coast
intro: South of Hua Hin, the coast softens into pine-fringed beaches, fishing villages and some of Thailand's most discreet boutique resorts. Pranburi rewards the extra half hour on the road with space, silence and limestone headlands on the horizon.

paragraphs: Your chauffeur follows Rama II Road and then Phetkasem Road, Highway 4, through Phetchaburi and past Hua Hin before turning towards the coast at Pranburi. The distance is roughly 230 km, and the journey takes approximately three and a half hours.

That is long enough to warrant a pause. Most guests stop once, either for coffee near Phetchaburi or for lunch in Hua Hin, before the final, quieter stretch to the resorts strung along the Pak Nam Pran and Khao Kalok shoreline.

Pranburi has largely avoided high-rise development. Instead you find low-slung villas, beach houses set back behind casuarinas, and small restaurants serving the day's catch. It is a favourite of Bangkok residents who want a private weekend rather than a scene.

Nature is the main attraction. Pranburi Forest Park has a boardwalk through mangroves, and Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park, further south, is home to Phraya Nakhon Cave, where a royal pavilion sits beneath a natural skylight. Sam Phraya Beach inside the park is usually close to deserted on weekdays.

Kite-surfers come for the steady seasonal winds, birdwatchers for the marshes of Sam Roi Yot, and everyone else for long, unhurried lunches overlooking the Gulf. It is the kind of place where an evening plan rarely extends beyond choosing which beach to watch the sunset from.

Pranburi is priced on our long-distance tier. Most guests take a one-way transfer and book the return separately, while some choose the day-trip rate to visit Sam Roi Yot with the chauffeur waiting at the trailhead. The rate table below shows both options.

Because resorts here can be some distance apart and taxis are scarce, it is worth arranging local transport in advance. Message us on WhatsApp with your plans and we will advise what makes sense for your stay.

h1: Bangkok to Rayong, business or beach
intro: Rayong is two places in one: the industrial heart of Thailand's Eastern Economic Corridor and a laid-back coast of fruit orchards and fishing beaches. Whether you are visiting a plant at Map Ta Phut or a beach house at Mae Phim, the drive is smooth and straightforward.

paragraphs: Your chauffeur takes Motorway 7 out of Bangkok towards Chonburi and Laem Chabang, then continues on the motorway or Highway 36 to bypass central Pattaya. For approximately 180 km, allow around two and a half to three hours.
Highway 36 is the key here: it keeps you clear of Pattaya's congested Sukhumvit Road and brings you into Rayong at speed. Service areas on Motorway 7 make a comfortable halfway pause if you need one.

Rayong is home to Map Ta Phut and a string of industrial estates serving the automotive, petrochemical and energy sectors. Executives often need to reach a site meeting on time, review documents en route and return to Bangkok the same evening.

A quiet Camry or an Alphard Executive with reclining seats turns those six hours of round-trip driving into usable working time. With the day-trip rate, your chauffeur waits on site and is ready the moment your meeting ends.

Our chauffeurs are used to industrial-estate routines: gate passes, visitor car parks and site safety rules. Tell us the estate and the building when you book, and we will plan the approach so that you arrive at the right entrance rather than circling the perimeter road looking for it.

Away from industry, Rayong has a gentle, local feel. Laem Mae Phim and Hat Mae Ramphueng are long beaches favoured by Thai families, and the province is famous for its durian, mangosteen and rambutan orchards, many of which welcome visitors in season, usually around May and June.
Rayong is also the gateway to Koh Samet via Ban Phe Pier. If you are heading to the island, see our Koh Samet page, where we explain the pier drop-off and ferry options.

Rayong is priced on our long-distance tier: choose a one-way transfer or a full day trip. Fuel, tolls and the chauffeur are always included. Send your address and timings on WhatsApp and we will confirm the vehicle.

If you are combining business and leisure, a common pattern is a site visit on Friday followed by a weekend on the coast, with a separate return booked for Sunday evening or Monday morning.

h1: Bangkok to Koh Samet, pier to paradise
intro: Koh Samet is the closest island escape to Bangkok with genuinely white sand and clear water. We drive you to Ban Phe Pier on the Rayong coast, timed for your ferry or speedboat, so the only queue you meet is the one for the boat.

paragraphs: Cars do not travel to Koh Samet, so the transfer has two stages. Your chauffeur drives you approximately 200 km from Bangkok to Ban Phe Pier, usually via Motorway 7 and Highway 36, in around three hours. At the pier, he helps you with luggage to the ticket counter or straight to your boat.

From Ban Phe, regular passenger ferries cross to Na Dan Pier on the island in roughly 40 minutes, while speedboats take around 15 to 20 minutes and can drop you at the beach in front of many resorts. Several piers operate along the Ban Phe waterfront, so tell us which one your resort uses.

Ferries are inexpensive and run frequently during the day, but schedules thin out in the late afternoon. Speedboats cost more and can be chartered privately, which suits families with a lot of luggage or anyone arriving after the last regular boat.

Many island resorts will arrange a speedboat transfer for you. If yours does, send us the boat time on WhatsApp and we will plan your departure from Bangkok so you arrive with a comfortable margin rather than a rush.

Koh Samet is part of a national park, and an entry fee is collected on arrival. Sai Kaew Beach is the liveliest, Ao Wong Duean is a sheltered crescent, and Ao Prao on the quieter west coast is known for sunsets and some of the island's more refined resorts.
Inland, the roads are rough and transport is by songthaew or rented scooter, which is why we recommend travelling light and letting the boat do the heavy lifting.

We can meet your boat at Ban Phe on the way back, with the car waiting near the pier. Koh Samet is priced on our long-distance tier, with fuel, tolls and the driver included; see the rate table below.

Because sea conditions can delay boats, your chauffeur keeps an eye on messages rather than a fixed clock. If your speedboat is running late, simply let us know on WhatsApp and the car will still be there when you step onto the pier.

Many guests also use the return drive for a final seafood lunch in Ban Phe or a stop at a Rayong fruit stall before reaching Bangkok in the early evening, rested and without having handled a single suitcase in a crowded bus station.

h1: Bangkok to Koh Chang, unhurried
intro: Koh Chang is Thailand's third-largest island, a mountain of rainforest rising from the sea near the Cambodian border. It is a long way from Bangkok, which is precisely why the journey deserves a comfortable private car and a chauffeur who knows the road to Trat.

paragraphs: Your chauffeur drives you approximately 315 km from Bangkok to the Laem Ngop area in Trat province, where the ferries to Koh Chang depart. The route typically follows Motorway 7 towards Chonburi, then Highway 36 and Sukhumvit Road, Highway 3, through Rayong and Chanthaburi. Allow around four and a half to five hours, including a rest stop.

At the coast, the car drops you at the ferry pier your plans require, usually Ao Thammachat or Centrepoint, both close to Laem Ngop. Vehicle ferries cross to the island in roughly 30 to 45 minutes, and you travel on board as a foot passenger with your luggage.

Koh Chang's ferry piers are on the north-east coast, while most resorts line the west coast along White Sand Beach, Klong Prao, Kai Bae and Lonely Beach. Many resorts arrange a pick-up from the island pier; if yours does, share the details with us and we will time your departure from Bangkok so you meet the ferry with a comfortable margin.

The island rewards slow travel. Klong Plu waterfall is an easy walk through the forest, Bang Bao in the south is a fishing village built on stilts over the water, and boat trips to the smaller islands of the archipelago leave from the southern coast.
Island roads are steep and winding between the beaches, so we recommend settling into your resort before exploring and using local taxis or your hotel's driver once there.

The alternatives are a long bus ride with a change in Trat, or a flight to Trat airport followed by a transfer. A private car keeps you on your own schedule, with legroom for five hours, a stop for lunch whenever you like and no luggage handling between vehicles until the ferry.

Families and groups will find an Alphard or Vellfire especially welcome on a journey of this length. Your chauffeur can also break the trip in Chanthaburi for its riverside quarter or cathedral, turning the transfer into a gentle half-day of sightseeing.

Because the distance and pier arrangements vary, Koh Chang transfers are quoted individually. Send us your date, pick-up address, group size and ferry or resort details on WhatsApp, and we will confirm a fixed price with fuel, tolls and the chauffeur included before you commit.
We can also arrange the return leg from the mainland pier, so the car is waiting when your ferry docks at the end of your stay.

title: Bangkok to Chanthaburi Private Chauffeur Transfer
metaDescription: Private chauffeur from Bangkok to Chanthaburi for gems, fruit orchards and the old riverside quarter. Price confirmed on WhatsApp, fuel and tolls included.
h1: Chanthaburi: gems, orchards and history
intro: Chanthaburi is one of the east's most rewarding and least crowded provinces, famous for its gem market, its fruit orchards and a French-era cathedral beside the river. It is an easy, scenic drive with a private chauffeur, and a fascinating place to spend a day or a weekend.

paragraphs: From Bangkok your chauffeur heads out on Motorway 7, continues past Laem Chabang on Highway 36 to bypass Pattaya, then joins Sukhumvit Road, Highway 3, through Rayong province to Chanthaburi. The distance is approximately 245 km, and the journey takes around three and a half to four hours.

The final stretch runs past durian and rambutan orchards and roadside stalls selling the season's fruit, so a brief stop is almost obligatory. Service areas on Motorway 7 and petrol-station cafés along Highway 3 make easy rest points.

If you set off early, you can reach Chanthaburi in time for a late breakfast at the riverside, explore the old quarter before the midday heat and spend the afternoon among the orchards or at the waterfall before heading home or onward to your hotel.

sections.h2: The gem market and the old town
paragraphs: Chanthaburi has been a centre of the gemstone trade for generations, and on weekends the streets around Sri Chan Road fill with dealers examining sapphires and rubies at folding tables. It is a remarkable sight even if you are not buying, and it is busiest from Friday to Sunday.

A short walk away, the Chanthaboon Waterfront community preserves wooden shophouses along the river, now home to cafés and small museums. Across the water stands the Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception, a Gothic Revival church often described as the largest Catholic cathedral in Thailand.

Fruit season, usually from around May to June, brings visitors to orchards that offer tastings of durian, mangosteen and longkong. Namtok Phlio National Park, a short drive from town, has a clear pool full of fish beneath a waterfall, and the mangrove bay of Khung Kraben has a long boardwalk and a well-presented learning centre.

h1: Bang Saen, Bangkok's nearest beach
intro: Bang Saen is where Bangkok goes for a breath of sea air. Around an hour and a half from the city, it has a long palm-lined beach, a hill full of monkeys and some of the best-loved seafood markets on the coast.

sections.h2: The quickest coast from the capital
paragraphs: Your chauffeur takes Motorway 7 east and leaves it near Chonburi, a drive of approximately 100 km that usually takes around an hour and a half. Highway 34, the Bang Na–Trat road, offers a back-up if the motorway is busy.

That short journey time is what makes Bang Saen special. You can leave after breakfast, spend the day by the sea and be home for dinner, which is why it is a favourite with Bangkok families and university students alike.

Bang Saen Beach stretches for several kilometres, lined with deckchairs, umbrellas and food vendors. At its northern end, Khao Sam Muk is a small hill with a shrine and a large troop of macaques, and a viewpoint over the bay. To the south, Wonnapa Beach is quieter, with a promenade popular for evening walks.

Ang Sila, a few minutes north, is a fishing community famous for its granite mortars and its seafood market, while Nong Mon Market is the place to buy dried seafood and Thai snacks to take home. The Bang Saen Aquarium, run by Burapha University's marine science institute, is a good stop with children.

In the evening, the beach road comes alive with grilled seafood stalls and families picnicking on mats under the casuarinas. It is a cheerful, very Thai scene and a world away from the resort polish of Pattaya, just half an hour further down the motorway.

sections.h2: A full day with your driver
paragraphs: Bang Saen is priced on our Eastern Seaboard tier, which includes up to ten hours with the car and chauffeur. That suits a relaxed day perfectly: beach in the morning, seafood lunch at Ang Sila, the aquarium after the midday heat and a sunset walk on Wonnapa before the drive home.
Your chauffeur stays close by throughout, so you can leave towels, shopping and a change of clothes in the car rather than carrying them around.

Weekends are lively and parking along the beach road fills quickly, which is another reason a dropped-off arrival is more pleasant than self-driving. Weekdays are noticeably calmer. Book on WhatsApp with your pick-up time and we will take care of the rest.

Bang Saen also hosts a street-circuit motor-racing festival on certain weekends, when roads around the beach close and hotels fill up. If your dates coincide, book early and let your chauffeur plan the approach around the closures.

h1: Sattahip, the coast beyond Pattaya
intro: Sattahip lies south of Pattaya, where the hotel towers give way to naval bases, fishing villages and some of the cleanest beaches on the Eastern Seaboard. It is also next door to U-Tapao Airport, which makes it a practical base for travellers flying in and out of the east.

paragraphs: Your chauffeur follows Motorway 7 from Bangkok towards Pattaya, then continues south on the motorway or Sukhumvit Road, Highway 3, past Jomtien and Na Jomtien to Sattahip. For approximately 180 km, allow around two and a half hours.

The final stretch is quieter than central Pattaya and passes Bang Saray, a small fishing village with good seafood restaurants on the water. It is a natural place to pause for lunch if you set off in the morning.

Because Sattahip is beyond the busiest part of Pattaya, your chauffeur will usually stay on the motorway as long as possible and avoid the slow city-centre stretch of Sukhumvit Road. That small detail can save a surprising amount of time on a Friday or during the high season.

sections.h2: A navy town with fine beaches
paragraphs: Sattahip is home to the Royal Thai Navy's main base, and several of its best beaches, such as Hat Sai Kaew and Nang Ram, are administered by the navy. They are cleaner and calmer than Pattaya's, though access rules apply and foreign visitors may need to show identification or travel with a Thai companion at some beaches.
Samae San, at the southern tip of Chonburi province, is a fishing community with boats to nearby islands for snorkelling and a growing number of seafood restaurants overlooking the water.

The pace here is decidedly local: naval families, fishing boats and simple beachfront restaurants rather than bars and beach clubs. That is exactly its appeal for travellers who want the sea without the scene.

Nong Nooch Tropical Garden, one of the region's best-known attractions, lies within Sattahip district, with themed gardens, a large orchid collection and cultural shows. Nearby, Khao Chi Chan displays a huge Buddha image inlaid in gold on a limestone cliff, an impressive sight in the late afternoon light.
Several of the Eastern Seaboard's well-regarded golf courses sit between Pattaya and Sattahip, so this route is popular with golfing groups who prefer staying away from the city centre.

h1: Khao Yai: forest, wine and fresh air
intro: Khao Yai is Bangkok's highland escape: a UNESCO-listed forest with wild elephants and gibbons, ringed by vineyards, farm stays and stylish resorts. The air is cooler, the pace slower and the drive surprisingly easy with a private chauffeur.

paragraphs: Your chauffeur leaves Bangkok northwards on Phahonyothin Road, Highway 1, then joins Mittraphap Road, Highway 2, through Saraburi to Pak Chong, the town at the foot of the park. The distance is approximately 180 km and the journey usually takes around two and a half to three hours.
Friday evenings and Sunday afternoons are the busiest times, as Bangkok residents head to their weekend houses. A mid-morning weekday departure is often the smoothest of all.

Khao Yai National Park forms part of the Dong Phayayen–Khao Yai Forest Complex, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Wild elephants are sometimes seen on the park roads, hornbills and gibbons in the canopy, and waterfalls such as Haew Suwat and Haew Narok are at their most powerful after the rains.

With your own car and driver you can move between viewpoints and trailheads at your own pace, which matters in a park this large. Many visitors hire a local ranger-guide for a walk, and your chauffeur will wait at the trailhead until you return.

The park can be busy with Thai visitors at weekends and on public holidays, particularly around the main waterfalls and viewpoints. A weekday visit, or an early start on a weekend, gives you far quieter trails and a much better chance of spotting wildlife along the roadside.

Outside the park, Khao Yai has become a leisure destination in its own right. PB Valley and GranMonte are vineyards that offer tours and tastings, Chokchai Farm is a long-established dairy farm popular with families, and Primo Piazza and Palio bring a playful Italian-village style to the hills.
The area's resorts range from forest lodges to design-led pool villas. A chauffeur makes wine tasting relaxed, too: nobody needs to drive afterwards.

Food is part of the experience, from farm cafés serving fresh milk and steak to fine-dining restaurants in the better resorts. Your chauffeur knows the area well and can suggest a lunch stop that suits your group.

h1: Nakhon Nayok, waterfalls within reach
intro: Nakhon Nayok is the green province Bangkok residents escape to when they want rivers, waterfalls and mountain views without a long journey. It sits at the southern edge of the Khao Yai massif, about two hours from the city, and makes an excellent private day trip.

sections.h2: Out of the city and into the green
paragraphs: Your chauffeur heads north to Rangsit and then east on Highway 305, a road that runs alongside the long, straight Rangsit canal through rice fields towards Nakhon Nayok. The distance is approximately 110 km and the drive takes around two hours, depending on traffic leaving Bangkok's northern suburbs.

As you approach the town, the hills of the Khao Yai range rise ahead, and the air already feels fresher. Roadside stalls along the way sell the province's well-known marian plums, called maprang, in season.

The province's best-known sights lie on the hillside north of town. Sarika Waterfall drops in several tiers through the forest, and Nang Rong Waterfall, with its picnic area and easy paths, is a family favourite. Wang Takrai, a riverside park laid out by a member of the royal family, has shaded lawns along a clear mountain stream.

Khun Dan Prakan Chon Dam holds back a broad reservoir framed by mountains, with a long crest road and viewpoints that are particularly beautiful in the late afternoon. For the more energetic, local operators run white-water rafting and kayaking trips on the Nakhon Nayok River, typically in the rainier months when the water is higher.

sections.h2: Cafés, resorts and the royal academy
paragraphs: Over recent years, Nakhon Nayok has become known for its riverside cafés and small resorts, many with views of the hills, which makes it a favourite for a long, leisurely lunch. The province is also home to the Chulachomklao Royal Military Academy, whose grounds include a museum.

Visiting all of this by public transport is tricky, because the attractions are spread along country roads with little regular service. With your own chauffeur, the day flows easily from waterfall to dam to café.

It is also a gentle introduction to rural Thailand for first-time visitors: orchards, temples and village markets line the back roads, and your chauffeur is happy to stop whenever something catches your eye.

h1: Ayutthaya, the old capital at leisure
kicker: Private Day Trip · 80 km · approx. 1.5 hrs
intro: For more than four centuries, Ayutthaya was the capital of Siam and one of the great cities of Asia. Its temple ruins, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site, lie about an hour and a half north of Bangkok, and a private chauffeur is easily the most comfortable way to see them.

paragraphs: Your chauffeur leaves the city on the elevated Don Mueang Tollway or Phahonyothin Road, Highway 1, continuing north past Rangsit and Bang Pa-in to Ayutthaya. The distance is approximately 80 km and the journey takes around an hour and a half, a little longer in morning rush hour.

Many visitors stop on the way at Bang Pa-in Palace, the royal summer residence with its lake, pavilions and an unusual mix of Thai, Chinese and European architecture. It is about 20 minutes short of Ayutthaya and works well as either the first or last stop of the day.

Ayutthaya's historical park spreads across an island ringed by rivers, with the main ruins too far apart to walk comfortably in the heat. Wat Mahathat is famous for the stone Buddha head entwined in tree roots, while the three great chedis of Wat Phra Si Sanphet stand beside the former royal palace grounds.

On the riverbank, Wat Chaiwatthanaram is perhaps the most photogenic of all, especially in the golden light of late afternoon. Wat Yai Chai Mongkhon, with its rows of saffron-robed Buddha images, and the vast reclining Buddha at Wat Lokayasutharam complete a classic circuit.

sections.h2: Why go with your own chauffeur
paragraphs: Organised coach tours follow a fixed timetable and often spend their best hours in transit. With a private car, you choose the order, linger where you like and retreat to a cool cabin between sites. Your chauffeur waits at each temple car park, so water, hats and shopping stay safely in the car.

Ayutthaya is priced on our Eastern Seaboard tier, which includes up to ten hours with the car. That is generous for a relaxed day with lunch by the river and a sunset at Wat Chaiwatthanaram before driving home.
Families appreciate the flexibility most. Children tire quickly in the heat, and being able to return to an air-conditioned Alphard for a rest between temples keeps the whole day pleasant.

Ayutthaya is known for its river prawns, grilled and served at restaurants along the water, and for roti sai mai, thin pancakes wrapped around strands of spun sugar, sold from stalls around the town. A riverside lunch is a highlight of the day.

If you would prefer to see the temples from the water, long-tail boats circle the island in the late afternoon, and your chauffeur can meet you at the landing afterwards. Book on WhatsApp and tell us which sights matter most to you.

h1: Lopburi: Khmer stones and monkey kings
intro: Lopburi is one of Thailand's oldest cities, layered with Khmer temples, a seventeenth-century royal palace and a resident population of long-tailed macaques. It is a memorable, slightly eccentric day out, and an easy one with a private chauffeur.

paragraphs: From Bangkok, your chauffeur drives north on Phahonyothin Road, Highway 1, past Ayutthaya province and on towards Lopburi, approximately 150 km in around two and a half hours. Many visitors combine the two cities in one long day, seeing Ayutthaya on the way up or the way back.
The road is straightforward and well served by fuel stations and cafés, so a comfort stop is never far away.

Phra Prang Sam Yot, three linked laterite towers built in the Khmer style, is Lopburi's emblem, and the hundreds of monkeys who live around it are its unofficial residents. Across the road, the San Phra Kan shrine is their headquarters. The monkeys are entertaining but bold, so keep bags zipped and sunglasses out of reach.

Phra Narai Ratchaniwet, the palace of King Narai in the seventeenth century, houses a national museum within thick old walls, and nearby Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat has a tall central prang and fine stucco work. Together they make a compact and fascinating historic quarter.

The town itself is compact, and your chauffeur can drop you at the edge of the old quarter and collect you on the other side, saving a hot walk back. Keep in mind that the monkeys sometimes clamber over parked cars, so windows stay closed and the car is parked a sensible distance from the temples.

From around November to January, the countryside around Lopburi is covered with sunflower fields in bloom, and farms open their gates to visitors for photographs. It is a cheerful sight and one that is very hard to reach without your own transport.

Further east, the Pa Sak Jolasid Dam creates a large reservoir with a long crest road and, at times, a small train service running across the dam. The scale of the landscape is a pleasant contrast to the dense old town.

intro: Kanchanaburi combines moving wartime history with some of western Thailand's most beautiful scenery. The Bridge on the River Kwai, the Death Railway and the turquoise pools of Erawan are all within reach, and a private chauffeur lets you see them without the rush of a coach tour.

paragraphs: Your chauffeur leaves Bangkok on Phetkasem Road, Highway 4, passing Nakhon Pathom and its great golden chedi, before turning north-west on Highway 323 to Kanchanaburi town. The distance is approximately 130 km and the journey takes around two and a half hours.

Nakhon Pathom makes a worthwhile short stop on the way, and roadside stalls along the route sell fruit and snacks. Once in Kanchanaburi, the landscape opens up into limestone hills, river valleys and sugar-cane fields.

On the return leg, your chauffeur can time the drive to avoid the late-afternoon build-up on Phetkasem Road as it enters Bangkok's western suburbs, which can add a surprising amount of time on Fridays and Sundays.

During the Second World War, prisoners of war and conscripted Asian labourers were forced to build a railway towards Burma, and many thousands died. The Bridge on the River Kwai, still in use today, is the best-known symbol of that history, and visitors can walk across it between trains.

The Kanchanaburi War Cemetery, immaculately maintained, lies in the centre of town, and the Thailand–Burma Railway Centre beside it explains the story with care. Further up the line, the Hellfire Pass Memorial and the timber viaduct near Tham Krasae are deeply affecting places to visit.

Erawan National Park, roughly an hour beyond town, is famous for its seven-tier waterfall with clear, mineral-blue pools where you can swim. The trail climbs steadily, and the upper tiers are much quieter than the first few.
Kanchanaburi is also known for its floating raft resorts on the River Kwai, which range from rustic to genuinely stylish. Many guests stay a night or two to enjoy the river at dawn and dusk.

Other natural highlights include Sai Yok Noi Waterfall, close to the railway, and the forested hills further west towards the Myanmar border. Elephant experiences are offered in the area too; if you plan to visit one, we suggest choosing a sanctuary that does not offer riding.

Kanchanaburi is priced on our long-distance tier. A day trip covering the bridge, the cemetery and one further site is perfectly achievable, while Erawan and Hellfire Pass together are better suited to an overnight stay. The rate table below shows both options.

title: Bangkok to Ratchaburi Private Transfer & Day Trip

h1: Ratchaburi: caves, ceramics and cool hills
intro: Ratchaburi is the province most visitors pass through on the way to the floating markets, yet it deserves a day of its own. Limestone caves, a long tradition of dragon-jar ceramics and the cool hills of Suan Phueng near the Myanmar border make it a varied and rewarding trip.

paragraphs: Your chauffeur leaves Bangkok on Phetkasem Road, Highway 4, passing Nakhon Pathom and continuing south-west to Ratchaburi town. The distance is approximately 100 km, and the journey usually takes around one and a half to two hours.

Because Ratchaburi province covers a wide area, the exact time depends on where you are going. Damnoen Saduak is on the eastern side; Suan Phueng is an hour or so west of town, up winding roads into the hills.

Tham Khao Bin is a cave of dramatic stalactites and stalagmites, lit to show its formations, and a short drive from town. Khao Ngu Stone Park surrounds a lake with limestone cliffs and caves that hold ancient Buddha images carved into the rock.
In Photharam district, Wat Khanon is renowned for its collection of nang yai, the large leather shadow puppets of classical Thai theatre, and for occasional performances of this rare art.
These sites are spread across the province and often reached on quiet rural roads with little signage in English, so a chauffeur who knows the area saves a great deal of time and guesswork.

Ratchaburi is famous across Thailand for its glazed ceramic jars decorated with coiling dragons. Several workshops welcome visitors to watch potters at work and to paint or buy pieces, which makes for a memorable and genuinely local stop.

To the west, Suan Phueng has become a popular retreat with cool mornings, mountain views and an array of themed resorts and farm cafés. It is a favourite with Bangkok families and couples for a quiet night away from the city. The roads up are narrow and winding, so a steady, experienced driver and a comfortable cabin make a real difference to how you arrive.

Ratchaburi is priced on our long-distance tier: choose a one-way transfer, for instance to a Suan Phueng resort, or a full day trip with your chauffeur waiting at each stop. Fuel, tolls and the driver are always included; see the rate table below.

A popular plan combines Damnoen Saduak Floating Market early in the morning with the caves and a ceramics workshop later in the day. Your chauffeur will suggest a sensible order, keeping driving to a minimum and making sure you are back in Bangkok in good time.

title: Damnoen Saduak Floating Market Private Day Trip
metaDescription: Private chauffeur from Bangkok to Damnoen Saduak Floating Market and Maeklong Railway Market. Fixed price, fuel, tolls and 10 hours included.
h1: Damnoen Saduak, before the crowds arrive
intro: Damnoen Saduak is Thailand's most famous floating market, a maze of canals where vendors paddle boats piled with fruit, noodles and flowers. The secret to enjoying it is arriving early, and a private chauffeur is the simplest way to be there as the first boats set out.

paragraphs: Damnoen Saduak lies approximately 100 km south-west of Bangkok, in Ratchaburi province. Your chauffeur usually takes Rama II Road or Phetkasem Road, Highway 4, depending on your pick-up point and the morning traffic, and the drive takes around one and a half to two hours.

The market is liveliest from early morning until late morning, after which the tour coaches arrive in force and the canals become crowded. Leaving Bangkok around 6.30am lets you board a boat at around 8am, when the light is soft and the vendors are setting up.

Visitors explore the canals by paddle boat or motorised long-tail, hired from the piers along the main canal. Boat prices are set by the operators rather than by us, and it is worth agreeing the duration and route before you set off.

Look out for boat noodles served straight from the water, coconut pancakes, mango with sticky rice and the vendors' wide-brimmed straw hats. Away from the main canal, quieter side channels show the wooden houses and orchards that still line the waterways.

sections.h2: Combine it with the railway market
paragraphs: Maeklong Railway Market, roughly half an hour away in Samut Songkhram, is where stallholders fold back their awnings each time a train edges through the market. Train times vary, so your chauffeur will check the day's schedule and plan the visit around it.

Later in the day, Amphawa's weekend floating market comes to life, and Wat Bang Kung, a small temple enclosed by the roots of a banyan tree, is a short drive away. A coconut-sugar farm, where palm sap is boiled down in large woks, makes another genuine local stop.

title: Bangkok to Amphawa Floating Market Private Trip
metaDescription: Private chauffeur from Bangkok to Amphawa's weekend floating market and firefly boats. Fixed price, fuel, tolls and 10 hours included. Book on WhatsApp.
h1: Amphawa, where the canals glow
kicker: Private Day Trip · 75 km · approx. 1.5 hrs
intro: Amphawa is the floating market Thais themselves love most: a riverside town of wooden houses, canal-side cafés and seafood grilled on boats. It comes alive on weekend afternoons and evenings, and ends with boat rides to see fireflies glittering in the trees.

paragraphs: Amphawa lies in Samut Songkhram province, approximately 75 km south-west of Bangkok. Your chauffeur takes Rama II Road, Highway 35, through salt flats and fish farms, and the journey usually takes around an hour and a half.
Rama II can be slow at peak times, so we plan around the traffic. For an afternoon visit, leaving Bangkok around midday or early afternoon brings you into Amphawa as the market warms up.

Unlike Damnoen Saduak, Amphawa is at its best later in the day, and mainly from Friday to Sunday. Stalls line both banks of the canal, selling sweets, crafts and souvenirs, while boats moored at the steps grill prawns, squid and scallops to order.

As dusk falls, long-tail boats set off to look for fireflies in the lamphu trees along the river. How many you see depends on the season and the weather, but on a good evening the effect is enchanting. Many of these boat tours also pass illuminated riverside temples.

Between the stalls, look for the old wooden shophouses that have been turned into cafés and guesthouses, many with small balconies over the water. Finding a table there for a drink as the lanterns come on is one of the nicest moments of the day.

Maeklong Railway Market, a few minutes away, is one of the most extraordinary sights in Thailand: a working market spread across the railway line, with awnings folded back for each passing train. Wat Bang Kung, whose small chapel is wrapped in banyan roots, and the King Rama II Memorial Park, celebrating the poet-king born nearby, are both worth a visit.
Don Hoi Lot, at the mouth of the Maeklong River, is known for its razor-clam beds and seafood restaurants, and is at its most interesting at low tide.

Amphawa is priced on our Eastern Seaboard tier, which includes up to ten hours with the car and chauffeur. A natural plan is an early-afternoon departure, the railway market and Wat Bang Kung, the floating market at dusk and a firefly boat before the drive home.

Returning late at night is effortless with your own driver, and you can simply sleep in the back. If you would rather stay over in a riverside homestay, take the one-way option and we will collect you the next day. Book on WhatsApp.

Because the market is busiest on Saturday evenings, your chauffeur will drop you close to the canal and arrange a clear meeting point, so you are not searching for the car among the crowds afterwards.

Firefly boat rides at dusk
Seafood grilled on boats at the canal steps
Maeklong Railway Market a few minutes away

tips: Visit Friday to Sunday; on weekdays the market is very quiet.
Plan to arrive around 3pm and stay until after dark for the firefly boats.
Bring mosquito repellent for the evening boat ride.
Visit Don Hoi Lot at low tide to see the clam beds exposed.

h1: Chachoengsao, a city of faith and rivers
kicker: Private Day Trip · 80 km · approx. 1.5 hrs
intro: Chachoengsao, on the banks of the Bang Pakong River, draws pilgrims from across Thailand to its revered temples and its giant reclining Ganesha. It is close enough for a relaxed half or full day, and full of the kind of local colour that coach tours rarely reach.

paragraphs: Chachoengsao lies approximately 80 km east of central Bangkok. Your chauffeur usually takes Motorway 7 or the Bang Na–Trat road, Highway 34, before turning north towards the city, a drive of around an hour and a half.
Because it sits just off the main Eastern Seaboard routes, Chachoengsao can also be combined with a trip to Bang Saen or a stop on the way to Pattaya, given an early start.
The final approach crosses flat, fertile countryside of rice fields, canals and fish ponds, a reminder of how quickly the city gives way to rural Thailand on this side of Bangkok.

Wat Sothon Wararam Worawihan is one of the most visited temples in Thailand, home to the deeply revered Luang Pho Sothon Buddha image. Its modern ordination hall is vast and gleaming white, and the temple grounds are busy with worshippers offering flowers and incense, especially at weekends.

A short drive away, Wat Saman Rattanaram is known for its enormous reclining pink Ganesha beside the river. Devotees whisper their wishes to small rat statues at its feet, believed to carry the message to the deity. It is colourful, cheerful and unlike any other temple most visitors will see.

Ban Mai, a riverside market in the city that has been trading for over a hundred years, preserves wooden shophouses and old-fashioned Chinese-Thai coffee shops. It is a pleasant place for lunch and a slow wander. Not far away, Khlong Suan Market, another century-old waterside market, offers similar charm with traditional snacks and toys.
Along the Bang Pakong River, restaurants serve river prawns and local dishes with views of the water, a fine way to end the day before heading back to Bangkok.

Chachoengsao is priced on our Eastern Seaboard tier, which includes up to ten hours with the car and chauffeur. That is generous for this itinerary, leaving room for both temples, a market lunch and a riverside dinner, or for an onward stop on the coast.

h1: Nakhon Pathom, beneath the great chedi
intro: Nakhon Pathom is one of Thailand's oldest settlements, believed to be where Buddhism first took root in the region. Just west of Bangkok, it combines an immense golden chedi, a graceful royal palace and lively riverside markets in a comfortable day.

paragraphs: Nakhon Pathom lies approximately 60 km west of central Bangkok. Your chauffeur takes Borommaratchachonnani Road or Phetkasem Road, Highway 4, and the drive usually takes around an hour to an hour and a half, depending on traffic crossing the river.
Its closeness makes it ideal for travellers who want a taste of provincial Thailand without a long journey, or who are already heading west towards Kanchanaburi, Ratchaburi or the floating markets.

sections.h2: The great chedi and the palace
paragraphs: Phra Pathom Chedi dominates the town, a bell-shaped stupa of orange-gold tiles that is often described as the tallest in Thailand. Its broad terraces, cloisters and small museum reward an unhurried visit, and the surrounding market is a good place to try local snacks, including the province's renowned pomelos when in season.

Sanam Chandra Palace, built by King Rama VI, sits in landscaped grounds with a striking mix of Thai and European architecture, including a half-timbered building that would not look out of place in an English village. It is a peaceful, shaded place to walk.

The chedi is especially atmospheric in the early evening, when the tiles glow in the low sun and families gather on the lawns. If you are staying for dinner, your chauffeur can suggest a local restaurant before the short drive back.

Don Wai Market, on the Tha Chin River, is a bustling riverside market known for its braised duck, sweets and river cruises. In Sam Phran, the Sampran Riverside estate, long known as the Rose Garden, offers organic farm visits, cooking classes and cultural demonstrations in landscaped gardens.
Nearby, the Thai Human Imagery Museum displays strikingly lifelike figures of monks and scenes from Thai life, an unusual but memorable stop.

Nakhon Pathom is priced on our outskirt Bangkok tier, which includes up to ten hours with the car and chauffeur. That leaves plenty of time for the chedi, the palace and a riverside lunch, with room for one further stop on the way back into the city.

Your chauffeur waits at each site, which is especially welcome when visiting temples that require you to remove your shoes and cover up in the heat. Fuel, tolls and the driver are included; see the rate table below.

Many guests use Nakhon Pathom as a gentle first excursion on their trip, a chance to see temples and markets away from the crowds of Bangkok's old town. Book on WhatsApp with your hotel and preferred start time.

h1: Samut Prakan, just beyond the city
kicker: Private Day Hire · 30 km · 45 min–1 hr
intro: Samut Prakan begins where Bangkok's south-eastern suburbs meet the Gulf of Thailand. Within an hour of the city centre you find the vast open-air museum of the Ancient City, the towering three-headed elephant of the Erawan Museum and the green, car-free lanes of Bang Krachao.

paragraphs: Samut Prakan lies approximately 30 km from central Bangkok. Depending on where you are going, your chauffeur takes Sukhumvit Road, the Bang Na–Bang Pakong expressway or the expressway network south across the river, and the drive usually takes around 45 minutes to an hour.
The province also surrounds Suvarnabhumi Airport, so its attractions are a convenient way to fill a free day before a late departure, with your luggage safely in the car.

The Ancient City, known in Thai as Muang Boran, is a huge outdoor park shaped roughly like the map of Thailand, filled with full-size and scaled replicas of the country's great temples and palaces. It is so large that visitors usually drive or cycle between the sites, which makes a chauffeur particularly useful.

The Erawan Museum is unmistakable from the road: a giant copper-clad three-headed elephant standing on a building that houses an ornate interior of stained glass, sculpture and antiques. It is a short, striking visit that fits easily into any day.

Bang Krachao, often called Bangkok's green lung, is a loop of the Chao Phraya River left largely to orchards, mangroves and raised cycle paths. Sri Nakhon Khuean Khan Park, a public park and botanical garden, is the place to walk among birds and ponds, and the weekend floating market at Bang Nam Phueng is a cheerful local scene.

On the coast, Bang Pu is famous for the flocks of seagulls that winter there, roughly from November to April, and for its seaside pier and promenade. Phra Samut Chedi, a white chedi on the river near the mouth of the Chao Phraya, is the provincial emblem.

Cycling is the best way to explore Bang Krachao's raised paths, and bicycles can be hired near the piers. Your chauffeur can drop you at one end and collect you later, so there is no need to retrace your route.

Samut Prakan is priced on our outskirt Bangkok tier, which includes up to ten hours with the car and chauffeur. That is more than enough to combine the Ancient City, the Erawan Museum and Bang Krachao, or to pair sightseeing with shopping at the large malls of Bang Na.
